title: Myth vs Fact: "We patched, so we're safe" - the BeyondTrust zero-day (CVE-2026-102764)
description:
Myth vs Fact: three myths about the BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, CVE-2026-102764.

BeyondTrust Remote Support is the tool many help desks use to take control of a computer remotely. An authentication bypass let remote, unauthenticated attackers skip the login. BeyondTrust scores it 9.3 (CVSS 4.0, critical); Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier is affected.

Myth 1: "If it's not public, no one is using it." Fact: the first known compromises date to August 29, 2026. BeyondTrust contained a hosted compromise on September 28, says all Remote Support cloud (SaaS) customers were patched by October 9, disclosed on October 15, and the US agency CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 16.

Myth 2: "Once you patch, you're safe." Fact: patching does not remove persistence. Mandiant (Google) says the attackers deployed a web shell, escalated to root, attempted to extract credentials from the credential vault and set up persistence. Mandiant attributes the activity to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected China-nexus espionage actor.

Myth 3: "No alerts means no intruders." Fact: the attackers deleted logs, and BeyondTrust warns that an absence of known indicators does not establish that an appliance is uncompromised.

If your organisation runs it: patch self-hosted servers (BT26-05-RS; versions older than 24.3.1 must upgrade first), hunt for signs of compromise even after patching, rotate stored credentials, and forward appliance logs to an outside system such as a SIEM.

Sources
- Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, Alert AL26-025 (October 16, 2026): https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/al26-025-critical-vulnerability-impacting-beyondtrust-remote-support-cve-2026-102764
- BeyondTrust security advisory BT26-05: https://www.beyondtrust.com/trust-center/security-advisories/bt26-05
- Rapid7 (October 19, 2026): https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-102764-critical-beyondtrust-remote-support-authentication-bypass-exploited-in-the-wild
- BleepingComputer (October 16, 2026): https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/beyondtrust-patches-zero-day-exploited-in-attacks-since-august/
- Rescana (CISA KEV entry details): https://www.rescana.com/post/beyondtrust-remote-support-cve-2026-102764-kev

Narration uses an AI voice (ElevenLabs). Research, script and fact-check by Securidge.
